name: radare2 - CLI Reverse Engineering Framework
description: radare2 (and its fork rizin) is a command-line reverse-engineering framework: disassembler, hex editor, debugger, binary diffing, and scripting. Fast for triage, automation, and exploitation work - analyzing binaries, patching, finding gadgets, and debugging crashes from a terminal or over SSH.
notes:
=== OPEN + ANALYZE ===
  r2 -A <binary>         # open and run analysis (aaa)
  r2 -d <binary>         # open in debug mode

=== CORE COMMANDS (inside r2) ===
  aaa            # analyze all
  afl            # list functions
  s main ; pdf   # seek to main, print disassembly of function
  iz / izz       # strings in data / whole binary
  ii             # imports
  iI             # binary info (arch, bits, NX, PIC, canary)
  axt <addr>     # xrefs to
  V / VV         # visual / graph mode (p to cycle panes)

=== DEBUG ===
  r2 -d ./prog ; db <addr> (breakpoint) ; dc (continue) ; dr (registers)

=== EXPLOIT HELPERS ===
  /R pop rdi     # search ROP gadgets
  pxw @ <addr>   # examine memory
  woa / wx       # write/patch bytes

=== ONE-LINERS ===
  rabin2 -I <binary>     # security features (canary/nx/pic/relro)
  rabin2 -z <binary>     # strings

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  Ghidra        # GUI + decompiler
  gdb + pwndbg  # dynamic exploit dev
  objdump/readelf # quick static views

recommended.note: Ghidra for GUI decompilation of the same binary.
gdb for dynamic debugging of the target.

defense.why_it_works: radare2 parses standard executable formats and recovers disassembly, strings, imports, and control flow. Any shipped binary without hardening or obfuscation is fully analyzable offline.
defense.prerequisites: A copy of the target binary; optional execution for the debugger.
defense.impact: Fast triage of logic and vulnerabilities, gadget discovery for ROP chains, and binary patching.
defense.detection: Not detectable on the defender side (offline static/dynamic analysis). Hardening the binary is the mitigation.
defense.prevention: Compile with full mitigations (NX, PIE, RELRO, stack canaries, FORTIFY_SOURCE); strip symbols; obfuscate sensitive routines; keep security decisions server-side; monitor for exploit attempts (crashes/EDR) rather than the analysis itself.
